newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-SPANISH GIANTS DO BATTLE IN SUPER CUP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SPANISH GIANTS DO BATTLE IN SUPER CUP.

text.p: Perennial rivals Real Madrid and Barcelona will raise the curtain on a league season that they once again threaten to dominate when they play the first leg of the Spanish Super Cup on Wednesday.
Cup-holders Barcelona host the first match, with the return fixture on Saturday at the league champions' Bernabeu stadium in Madrid.
The giants of the Spanish game are expected to parade most of their impressive array of expensive summer signings.
Heading the list of new names are the managers of both sides.
But after mediocre pre-season campaigns, both Real's Jupp Heynckes and Barcelona's Louis van Gaal will be looking to convince fans that the multi-billion peseta spending spree was not in vain.
The Barcelona line-up should include Brazilian internationals Sonny Anderson and Rivaldo, who signed for four billion pesetas ($26.5 million) from Deportivo La Coruna on Friday.
Dutchmen Michael Reiziger and Ruud Hesp are also expected to start in a side that has been radically reshaped since Van Gaal took over in the close season.
Real Madrid did not plunge into the transfer market with quite as much enthusiasm as their rivals, but still bought seven new players from other Spanish clubs.
All eyes will be on how well Aitor Karanka, recently acquired from Athletic Bilbao, performs in the centre of the Madrid defence.
However Real will be without German international goalkeeper Bodo Illgner.
Illgner has a shoulder strain and his place will be taken by Jose Canizares.
With four wins in the last six seasons, Barcelona have made the Super Cup their own in recent years.
However Real Madrid have history on their side.
They have won all three previous Super Cup encounters between the two clubs since the competition began in 1982, their most recent victory coming in 1993.
Predictably neither manager is suggesting that the result will have much bearing on the league season, which starts on August 30th with the Real-Atletico derby match.
"The rivalry between Real Madrid and Barcelona is very important and it is always a big game between the two but to be realistic it is only a pre-season match," Heynckes said.
